trust_decision.summary: Decided in the login/logout success handlers: a post-auth redirect target supplied by the client (redirectUrl) is honoured only if it is a single-slash-anchored server-local path or an absolute URL matching the configured site host/protocol/port; otherwise the configured default target is used.

landing_point.why: This is the only pre-existing site at the pinned commit that contains a real same-site check, and its guard is the obvious defect: it skips validation entirely for any target starting with '/', so '//evil.example.com' is passed straight to sendRedirect (the classic protocol-relative bypass).

fix_sites.module_kind: Spring Security LogoutSuccessHandler in the jeeves/springutil module
new Spring Security AuthenticationSuccessHandler, activated by the bean wiring change

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper called from all four handlers
interactive Keycloak login completion with redirectUrl query parameter
OIDC/OAuth2 login completion with redirectUrl query parameter

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is a second logout-success handler in a different package (org.fao.geonet.web vs jeeves.config.springutil), takes a differently named parameter ('redirect' rather than 'redirectUrl'), and is only wired when geonetwork.security.type=cas, so it reads as a legacy CAS-only path outside the login redirectUrl contract the advisory describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-site absolute return targets (e.g. https://www.example.org/portal) are a supported behaviour and are deliberately accepted when host, protocol and port match the configured site; the default target also carries an @@nodeId@@ placeholder that is substituted afterwards. A fix that simply requires a leading '/' or rejects every absolute URL breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: server-local relative path with query string and fragment ('/geonetwork/srv/eng/catalog.search?a=b#/home')
absolute same-site URL matching host+protocol+port, including explicit port and implicit default port
absolute same-site URL differing only by host case
incomplete site configuration (null host, null protocol, null port)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /signout?redirect=<url> when the deployment uses the CAS profile: config-security-cas.xml overrides the core logoutSuccessHandler bean id and rebinds it to org.fao.geonet.web.RedirectLogoutSuccessHandler, which returns request.getParameter("redirect") verbatim (no validation at all) straight into sendRedirect.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a bean-id override inside a type-specific config file, so the fixed core handler looks like it still covers /signout; the parameter is named 'redirect', not 'redirectUrl'; and it only exists for the CAS security type, which the advisory summary does not mention.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (org.fao.geonet.web) and a different module (web/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/config-security) from the landing point; reachable only through config-security.xml:72 import selection

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a logout handler that honours a caller-supplied return target under the parameter name 'redirect'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: CAS single-logout needs to send the browser back to a caller-chosen page, so a maintainer would naturally add such a bean and enable Spring's targetUrlParameter.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: post-authentication redirect taken from the saved request / a return parameter on the Shibboleth backend
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every other auth backend in this repo (Keycloak, OIDC, form login) returns the user to the page they came from, so porting the same behaviour here is an obvious maintainer move.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Keycloak logout handler that forwards to an IDP logout URL and appends a caller-supplied return location
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already builds and redirects to an external IDP URL using a REDIRECT_PLACEHOLDER, so appending a request parameter there is a one-line change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: pre-auth filter that forwards a caller-supplied redirectUrl into the signin URL instead of deriving it from the request URI
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Its Keycloak twin already encodes a returningUrl into ?redirectUrl=, so accepting a supplied one instead is a plausible refactor.

O9_family: open_redirect (CWE-601, URL redirection to untrusted site)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module build (root pom.xml, no wrapper); maven-compiler-plugin source/target 11, maven-surefire-plugin 3.0.0-M5; module gn-core is where every affected class lives
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 4 + Mockito unit tests under core/src/test/java/org/fao/geonet/kernel/security/ (e.g. GeonetworkAuthenticationProviderIntegrationTest.java, jwtheaders/*Test.java, openidconnect/*Test.java). No tests existed for any redirect handler at the pinned commit; the fix adds three new test classes (RedirectUtilTest, GeonetworkSavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandlerTest, JeevesNodeAwareLogoutSuccessHandlerTest).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten each existing guard in place (require a leading '/' in the logout handler, keep !URI.isAbsolute() in the Keycloak/OIDC filters) - which drops the supported same-site absolute return target and still leaves the CAS /signout?redirect= handler open.

out_of_scope_notes: Other redirect code exists in this tree but is outside this advisory's protection and was not pursued: inspire-atom/src/main/java/org/fao/geonet/services/inspireatom/AtomGetData.java:152 (redirect to a URL taken from harvested metadata) and plugins/datahub-integration/src/main/java/org/fao/geonet/datahub/DatahubController.java:66-79 (redirect built from the request URI, so server-local).
